title: Cycle Shotgun Triage and Critical Skill Fencing Framework
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Create a lightweight mid-cycle decision framework for fast triage ("shotgun triage") that enables predictable scope cuts while explicitly protecting critical skill owners ("skill fencing").

Why: During recent cycles we repeatedly faced reactive scope freezes that eroded velocity because key engineers were pulled into fire drills. We need a repeatable process to make triage decisions in 48-72 hour windows that balances cycle-level OKRs with team-level capacity and reduces subjective rework.

Scope:
- Define a rapid scoring rubric for candidate scope cuts (impact, effort, regression risk, customer visibility).
- Create the skill-fencing policy to protect 1-2 critical roles per team per cycle unless explicit cross-team reallocation is approved.
- Build a triage cadence (who meets, artifacts required, decision SLA).
- Implement minimal console artifacts: a triage spreadsheet template and a dashboard card in the cycle planning board.
- Pilot with Platform and Runtime squads for one cycle.

Deliverables: triage rubric doc, fencing policy doc, playbook checklist, pilot retrospective notes, decision dashboard mockup, and a small automation to mark triage decisions on the cycle board.

Risks: incorrect fencing may create single points of failure; too-heavy process kills speed. Mitigations: strict 72-hour SLA, timeboxed meetings, and an escape hatch for emergency reassignments with CTO+PM approval.

Success metrics: reduction in unplanned engineer reassignments (-50% vs last cycle), time-to-decision for scope trims <72 hours, stakeholder satisfaction >=4/5 in pilot survey, and no regressions to critical OKRs during pilot.

acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc exists in Confluence with step-by-step triage flow and scoring rubric.
Skill-fencing policy clearly describes eligibility, duration, and approval flow and has at least two concrete examples.
Pilot executed for Platform and Runtime teams with one triage event and a retrospective recorded.
Automation ticket created to mark triage outcomes on the cycle board (or manual instructions documented).
Pilot metrics captured and baseline comparison completed (reassignments and time-to-decision).
proposed_steps: Finalize rubric and fencing definition (2 days)
Build triage spreadsheet template and dashboard mockup (3 days)
Run dry-run with cross-functional reps (1 day)
Execute pilot triage event in 2026-W12 (1 day)
Run pilot retrospective and capture metrics + decide next steps (2 days)
metrics: Unplanned engineer reassignments - count per cycle
Number of critical-path tasks left unaddressed after triage
Number of times fencing was overridden and reason logged
